assessments.reasoning: The complete text/MIT.txt came from the SPDX license-list-data repository at commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. Its 1,078-byte length and SHA-256 b05785f9f18e6716bab63424b11454513b9943a222595b70411009202fc592b5 matched the measured archive input, and the digest matched the claim's input pin. Its line breaks and placeholder line establish the claimed original byte interval. The CLI's digest-refusal case challenged whether changed source bytes could stand in for this input.

The complete json/details/MIT.json came from the same pinned SPDX commit, identified the license as MIT and had 8,433 bytes. Its SHA-256 0c2b3c87a154a4aaac6bc6a735dd454dc29d9a78c23a85deedb080e0c65de1f8 matched the reproduction's detail digest. Decoding licenseText restores the literal angle brackets, quotes, line breaks and final line feed visible in the plaintext. The runner directly tested whether that decoded field differed from the measured archive input and found byte equality. This supports its use as an exact representation of the input. The separate template and HTML fields played no part in that comparison.

limitations: The measurement covers one successful write with the specified commits, runtime, input, notice values and fresh destination. Other environments, inputs and destinations require their own evidence.
The fixture establishes no author permission, retention of existing project notices or right to redistribute license data.

The digest checks compare the acquisition-reported hashes with the frozen claim identity and the runner's independent source measurements. The supplied SCES-1.0 revision ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710 and bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce identify the assessment context. The acquisitions did not deliver the bundle for independent hashing.
reasoning: All three acquisitions returned complete UTF-8 bodies with HTTP 200 and no named subranges. The 2,002-byte revision 1 claim had the frozen claim digest. The reproduction matched its method SHA-256, 4ab610676414f43ec29dae882ce393c3ee187df2bb5e1b33cfc2c2d60fe07bcf, and ran public CLI commit 4c67e9b85e218fe40e9b17f2bde7fb90da0b552b on win32 with Python 3.13.5. With the verified 1,078-byte SPDX input, holder Example Project, year 2026 and a new scratch destination, the CLI wrote a file that the runner checked for exact contents. The measured file was 1,072 bytes with SHA-256 0196f81d7f82a887642e004cb0703c3069eb35bc493fdce129dd449f8ed092af. In the original plaintext, the title and two line feeds occupy bytes [0,13). The 40-byte placeholder notice occupies [13,53), with its terminating line feed at offset 53. The filled notice occupies 34 bytes. The six-byte reduction agrees with the measured length, and the exact-output check confirms preservation of the surrounding bytes. The runner recorded the write check separately from both preview checks.

reproduction.reason: The tool ran the real pinned CLI, verified a written scratch file, and matched the byte-level control.
